description: Short bounded-cycle RTL throughput benchmark, per claude_implementation_prompt.txt / this continuation's Section 4 ("Start with a short bounded benchmark (~200,000 cycles), measure actual throughput, save wall-clock timing, distinguish simulation time from compilation/startup").
ram_model: full (tb/ram_model.sv, the original -- tb/ram_model_lite.sv was NOT used for this benchmark; defines=[] during both runs below)
firmware: build/firmware/configs/case_full/firmware.elf (sha256 622d18164ee3c80540ca460547340246b989e689aad70ed714d4f59e8d192be5), unchanged logic from the previously recorded firmware (only the inert CASE_START/CASE_COUNT feature was added, defaulting to the full 20-case loop)

runs.purpose: Measure the compile+elaborate+startup wall-clock floor in isolation (10 RTL cycles is execution-negligible; this subprocess-based Zenith invocation recompiles/re-elaborates all sources on every run_simulation call, confirmed by the full compiler-warning preamble reappearing identically on every run)

Short bounded benchmark covering the firmware's early execution (TFLM init through roughly the middle of pre-Invoke() setup -- MMIO_TX markers '1','3','4','6' all observed, confirming correct init; HEARTBEAT at 50k/100k/150k/200k cycles shows PC and retired-instruction count advancing monotonically, i.e. genuine progress, not a hang)

computed_throughput.method: incremental: (bench_200k_001.wall_clock_seconds - bench_floor_001.wall_clock_seconds) / (200000 - 10), isolating compile/elaborate/startup overhead from actual per-cycle simulation cost

previously_recorded_value.source: the earlier 5,000,000-cycle probe run, RUN-firmware-rtl-001, see docs/issues.md ISS-004

comparison_to_previously_recorded_throug.caveat: These two measurements are NOT a controlled before/after comparison of the same code path -- this benchmark's 200,000 cycles cover only the firmware's early TFLM-initialization code (before Invoke() even starts at cycle 351185), whereas the earlier 5,000,000-cycle run's throughput reflects a mix of that same early code PLUS a large amount of actual Invoke()/MUL-heavy execution. The ~2x difference may reflect genuinely different simulator cost per RTL cycle depending on instruction/signal-activity mix (e.g. the sequential multiply/divide unit toggling more combinational logic per cycle during Invoke()), or may reflect other host-load variation between the two sessions; this was not isolated further. Both figures are reported as independently measured and should not be averaged or treated as interchangeable.
comparison_to_previously_recorded_throug.implication: No single 'cycles per second' figure should be used to project the total wall-clock time for completing Invoke() or the full 20-case run; any such projection must be treated as a rough estimate, not a measured figure.

ram_model_lite_speedup_measurement.description: Section 5's explicit before/after speedup requirement, measured once Animas MCP connectivity was restored and tb/ram_model_lite.sv was validated (see docs/decisions.md D-007). Same firmware (build/firmware/firmware.hex), same 200,000-cycle bound, same +HEARTBEAT=50000, trace=0, waveform off, in each pair.

ram_model_lite_runs.source: that run's own stderr line: "[zenith] simulated for 00:00:20  exit 0"

ram_model_lite_speedup_measurement.observed_speedup: ~30% wall-clock reduction (~1.43x): ~20s (lite) vs ~28.7s (full) for the same 200,000-cycle firmware segment, consistent across 2 samples per model
ram_model_lite_speedup_measurement.caveat: The two models' measurements come from different timing sources (Zenith's own internal timer for headless runs vs. the Animas daemon's start/done log timestamps for ui_remote_control runs) because run_simulation's execution mode was not caller-controlled and differed between calls. This is a real, reproducible difference, not a single isolated-variable measurement -- reported as an approximate ~30% improvement, not a precise figure.
ram_model_lite_speedup_measurement.functional_correctness_evidence: See docs/decisions.md D-007: random-program RETIRE trace exact match (default and injected-backpressure+randomized-latency timing) and full 9-directed-test regression, all under tb/ram_model_lite.sv, before this speedup number was relied on for anything.
